notes: Specific reading note: These are the recording’s 29 September 2025 examples, not dates prescribed for the present year.

At116.079s the native word is ariśina (turmeric); fine window3 instead recognizes aṣṭagandha, and the coarse pass has a noisy aṣṭanā join. Turmeric is retained from the explicit native marker; the divergent acoustic recognition is preserved in the clause audit.

The recorded ādya probably represents adya, today/now; its vowel remains uncertain. The bhautāvatāre dating-formula cluster is not securely parsed: bauddhāvatāre is a candidate, not a verified replacement or a confident material-incarnation claim. Recorded2025 dating/locality wording is preserved.
Specific reading note: mūḍisittu, the lamp-lighting expression varies slightly in the witnesses

The Kapila-Dattatreya verse contains audible restarts around the knowledge/fearlessness and Aja-assembly phrases. Both model passes and an independent targeted model are noisy there; the displayed phonetic joins remain provisional. No omitted continuation is supplied from a text.

The inserted pratihati fragment and the conch/rosary/understanding compound are phonetically variable across acoustic witnesses. The recitation ends after the Brahma/Isha phrase; the unspoken continuation in Tantrasara is not added.
The sun/moon joining phrase sounds ravīndum iti across witnesses. Its exact sandhi and the final great-praise phrase remain provisional.
Specific reading note: a short spoken cue between the salutation and invocation
The gem-comparison opening sounds harirmaṇi across witnesses; the reference text has darinmaṇi. The acoustic reading is retained rather than silently replacing it.
Specific reading note: Both acoustic passes read mattu, “again”; native captions read hattu.

The Narasimha prayer is present in both acoustic passes but its initial words lack separate usable native markers. That line replays the explicitly shared encompassing passage. The recited forms and dhyana compounds have noisy sandhi in the witnesses.

The discus/conch phrase is repeatedly restarted, and the faultless-power phrase repeats. The eight-forms fragment is retained where heard, without adding its reference-text continuation. Primary Tantrasara1.20 reads niḥśeṣaśaktimān, possessing complete/all powers. Native markers at527.360 and531.760 and fine window14/coarse window4 instead recognize nirdoṣa/niddhoṣa, faultless. The apparent spoken variant and both repetitions are retained; the primary-text difference is explicit rather than silently corrected.
The second meditation line is recovered by both acoustic passes despite omission/garbling in the captions. Its passage cue is shared where no separate reliable native lexical match survives.
The Bhu meditation is omitted from the coarse pass but retained by the fine pass and native captions. The blue-flower/betel and boon compound remains a provisional acoustic joining.
The conch/discus/trident compound and middle meditation line are noisy. The repeated discus-lotus wording is retained; exact inflections remain provisional.
The boon/fearlessness hand expression differs across the acoustic passes. The main Prana forms and the repeated invocation remain separately retained.

The meditation begins with a restart and repeats the perception and Self-knowledge phrases. Gauri’s one/two/four/eight/nine-footed sequence is recovered through the acoustic witnesses; some joining syllables remain provisional. The independent targeted model is also noisy, so no canonical pronunciation verification is claimed. Both acoustic passes retain an additional Bharati meditation-only echo; it is preserved with the shared684.079–686.880s range rather than silently removed.

The book-letter/luminous-line/Prana-Shri expression and the all-knowledge/excellence compound are disputed across both passes and the independent targeted model. Mahidasa and the favorable-presence verb are provisional lexical readings. The form and deity lists are fully retained. The prāṇaśrī cluster does not securely establish two deity names Prana and Shri; that proposed division remains unconfirmed.
The Jaganti, Svayampriti and Gugu/Kuhu-like deity names, and Jayatirtha’s contracted name, remain acoustic-name variants. The Janaki/Satya/Rukmini list restarts and is retained twice.

Noisy automatic readings have been corrected by comparing the retained acoustic clauses with Aitareya Brahmana3.24 and1.30. Kṣatra means sovereignty, not a canopy. Recorded repetitions and the final return to the foundation phrase remain. The final return’s exact gṛhāṇām inflection and api fragment are provisional. No surrounding canonical continuation has been added.
The offerings/arghya phrase is restarted and some endings vary. The image-to-book location correction is retained. Exact introductory gosvāmin wording remains provisional.

The native caption has three distinct presence-related expressions; the coarse pass omits one and the fine pass varies their order. All captioned occurrence slots are retained; the precise middle forms require further lexical review.
Specific reading note: the short connective around “coconut” is unclear

The Mula-nakshatra inflection and the joining between Saraswati, Bharati, Mukhyaprana and Lakshmi-Vedavyasa are provisional acoustic forms. This is the recording’s dedication, not a newly composed formula.
